definitions.explanation: A crane made by folding paper using the traditional Japanese art of origami. One of the most iconic origami shapes, strongly associated with wishes for peace and recovery from illness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{千羽鶴|せんばづる}→千羽鶴：30425_senbazuru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{折|お}り{鶴|づる}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{折|お}り→折る：01263_oru⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧た。
examples.english: I kept folding paper cranes to make a thousand-crane chain.

examples.japanese: {入院中|にゅういんちゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{折|お}り{鶴|づる}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}って→送る：00742_okuru⟧、⟦{回復|かいふく}→回復：03812_kaifuku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{祈|いの}った→祈る：01198_inoru⟧。
examples.english: I sent paper cranes to my friend in the hospital, praying for their recovery.

notes:
{折|お}り{鶴|づる} is one of the most recognized origami figures in Japanese culture. It is deeply connected to the tradition of folding ⟦{千羽鶴|せんばづる}→千羽鶴：30425_senbazuru⟧ (one thousand paper cranes), which are given as a prayer for recovery from illness or as a wish for peace.

CULTURAL NOTE: The tradition of ⟦{千羽鶴|せんばづる}→千羽鶴：30425_senbazuru⟧ became internationally known through the story of Sadako Sasaki, a girl who developed leukemia from the Hiroshima atomic bombing and folded paper cranes while hospitalized. {折|お}り{鶴|づる} are now a symbol of peace at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial.
